learningObjectives.title: Evolution and composition of the atmosphere

questions.q: What is the approximate percentage of nitrogen in the Earth's atmosphere today?
questions.explain: Nitrogen makes up about four-fifths (78%) of today's atmosphere, making it the most abundant gas.

questions.q: What is the approximate percentage of oxygen in the Earth's atmosphere today?
questions.explain: Oxygen makes up about one-fifth (21%) of the modern atmosphere.

questions.q: Which gas is thought to have made up most of the Earth's early atmosphere?
questions.explain: The early atmosphere was mainly carbon dioxide, similar to the atmospheres of Mars and Venus today.

questions.q: What was the main source of the gases in the Earth's early atmosphere?
questions.explain: Gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapour were released by intense volcanic activity as the Earth formed.

questions.q: How did the Earth's oceans form?
options: Water vapour condensed as the Earth cooled
Oxygen reacted with hydrogen in the air
Ice from comets melted in volcanoes
questions.explain: As the Earth cooled, water vapour in the atmosphere condensed to form the oceans.

questions.q: Which organisms first produced oxygen and increased its level in the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Algae, and later plants, produced oxygen through photosynthesis, gradually raising oxygen levels.

questions.q: Which processes helped reduce the amount of carbon dioxide in the early atmosphere?
options: Dissolving in the oceans and photosynthesis
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide dissolved in the oceans (forming carbonate sediments) and was taken up by photosynthesising organisms.

questions.q: Which equation correctly represents photosynthesis?
questions.explain: In photosynthesis carbon dioxide and water form glucose and oxygen: 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2.

questions.q: Which pair of gases are the main greenhouse gases linked to human activity?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide and methane are greenhouse gases whose increasing levels contribute to climate change.

questions.q: Which toxic gas is produced by the incomplete combustion of fuels?
questions.explain: Incomplete combustion in a limited oxygen supply produces the toxic, colourless gas carbon monoxide.

questions.q: Why is carbon monoxide dangerous to humans?
options: It binds to haemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport in the blood
It dissolves in water to form acid rain
It reacts with skin to cause burns
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin in red blood cells, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.

questions.q: Sulfur dioxide released when fuels are burned causes which environmental problem?
questions.explain: Sulfur dioxide, formed from sulfur impurities in fuels, dissolves in rainwater to produce acid rain.

questions.q: A car engine runs at very high temperature. Which pollutant forms when gases already present in the air react together in the engine?
questions.explain: At high temperatures, nitrogen and oxygen from the air react inside the engine to form oxides of nitrogen.

questions.q: What harmful effect is associated with carbon particulates (soot) released when fuels burn?
options: Acid rain and corrosion of metal
questions.explain: Particulates reflect sunlight causing global dimming and can cause respiratory problems when breathed in.

questions.q: What is meant by potable water?
options: Water that is safe to drink
Water that contains no dissolved oxygen
Water taken directly from the sea
questions.explain: Potable water is water that is safe to drink; it is not necessarily chemically pure.

questions.q: A water company treats fresh water from a reservoir. Which sequence of steps is used?
questions.explain: Fresh water is first filtered to remove solids, then sterilised (for example with chlorine) to kill microbes.

questions.q: Why is potable water usually not the same as pure water?
options: It still contains dissolved substances such as salts
It has been boiled and then cooled
It contains no oxygen at all
It has a lower boiling point than pure water
questions.explain: Potable water may contain dissolved minerals and salts, so it is safe to drink but not chemically pure.

questions.q: Which method is used to sterilise water and kill microbes during treatment?
questions.explain: Sterilising agents such as chlorine (as well as ozone or UV light) are used to kill microbes in water.

questions.q: A hydrocarbon fuel is burned in a limited supply of oxygen. In addition to water, which product is most likely to form?
questions.explain: A limited oxygen supply causes incomplete combustion, producing carbon monoxide (and sometimes soot) as well as water.

questions.q: A student needs pure water from a sample of salty seawater. Which method should be used?
questions.explain: Desalination by distillation evaporates the water and condenses it, leaving the dissolved salts behind.
